source.note: The orchestrator runs on every request and medium was its second empty cell. Reuses `refactor-config`, whose own task note records that this exact fixture already caught an orchestrator doing the implementation itself in manual-workflow mode rather than delegating -- 'the orchestrator did the work itself and no coder turn was ever taken' -- so the shape here targets that documented failure directly rather than inventing a new one. `delegates-implementation` requires a delegating tool in the console turn list and forbids `edit`/`write` there, which is the orchestrator's OWN top-level tool calls, not the Coder's -- the pass sample's tool list carries `run_role`/`run_step`/`choose_transition` and no `edit`, mirroring how `orchestrator-tool-use-v1`'s pass sample never lists the delegated coder's file edits either. `summary-carries-the-preserved-behavior` is the rule-into-a-downstream-artifact half of the medium definition: the constraint that separates this task from a trivial one-line fix -- both public functions keep their exact behaviour -- has to survive into what the orchestrator reports back to the operator, not stay implicit in an internal plan.
